response.basis: Extraction from numbered NL segments NL1-NL10 describing a train door/motion control state machine: root scope transitions DoorsClosing->InMotion->{Stopping,EmergencyStopping}, EmergencyStopping actions/effects, InMotion substates Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching with their own transitions, entry actions, and continuous behavior in Approaching.

contracts.basis: NL1 first clause 'The system starts in the DoorsClosing state'.

binding_hints.reason: The system is the enclosing scope owning the initial edge.
DoorsClosing is the state entered by the initial edge.

contracts.normative_statement: The root scope must have an initial pseudostate edge entering DoorsClosing.
contracts.quote: The system starts in the DoorsClosing state
contracts.reason: NL1 explicitly states the system starts in DoorsClosing, establishing a root-level initial entry.

binding_hints.reason: DoorsClosing is the stated transition origin.
InMotion is the stated transition destination.

contracts.normative_statement: DoorsClosing must transition to InMotion.
contracts.quote: transitions to InMotion when the doors are closed, triggered by the "Closed/SendDeparted" signal
contracts.reason: NL1 states an explicit transition from DoorsClosing to InMotion.

binding_hints.reason: InMotion is the shared source of the alternatives.
Stopping is the first alternative target.

contracts.normative_statement: InMotion must transition to Stopping on arrival.
contracts.quote: the system can either transition to the Stopping state when it arrives, indicated by the "Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived" signal
contracts.reason: NL2 states an alternative transition from InMotion to Stopping upon arrival.

binding_hints.reason: InMotion is the shared source of the alternatives.
EmergencyStopping is the second alternative target.

contracts.normative_statement: InMotion must transition to EmergencyStopping when an obstacle is detected.
contracts.quote: or to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected
contracts.reason: NL2 states an alternative transition from InMotion to EmergencyStopping on obstacle detection.

binding_hints.reason: Shared source of the two alternatives.

contracts.normative_statement: The InMotion alternatives to Stopping and EmergencyStopping must be distinguishable by their triggering conditions.
contracts.quote: the system can either transition to the Stopping state when it arrives ... or to the EmergencyStopping state if an obstacle is detected
contracts.reason: NL2 presents two mutually exclusive alternatives (arrival vs obstacle) from the same source, requiring distinguishable conditions.

contracts.normative_statement: EmergencyStopping must perform the Emergency Stop action.
contracts.quote: the system enters the EmergencyStopping state, which includes the actions "Emergency Stop"
contracts.reason: NL3 requires EmergencyStopping to include the Emergency Stop action; no exact lifecycle phase is stated.

contracts.normative_statement: EmergencyStopping must send the Obstacle Detected signal.
contracts.quote: sends the "Obstacle Detected" signal
contracts.reason: NL3 separately requires EmergencyStopping to send the Obstacle Detected signal, distinct from the Emergency Stop action.

contracts.normative_statement: InMotion must contain Accelerating as a substate.
contracts.quote: Within the InMotion state, the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching
contracts.reason: NL4 explicitly lists Accelerating as a substate of InMotion.

contracts.normative_statement: InMotion must contain Cruising as a substate.
contracts.quote: Within the InMotion state, the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching
contracts.reason: NL4 explicitly lists Cruising as a substate of InMotion.

contracts.normative_statement: InMotion must contain Approaching as a substate.
contracts.quote: Within the InMotion state, the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching
contracts.reason: NL4 explicitly lists Approaching as a substate of InMotion.

contracts.basis: NL4 'three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching'.

binding_hints.reason: Named list also could be read as explicit named members; primary reading chosen is direct_child_states since NL directly counts child states.

cardinality_requirement.alternative_reading: explicit_named_members (the same three named states read as a finite enumerated list rather than a general child-state count)
cardinality_requirement.basis: NL4 'the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching'.
cardinality_requirement.reason: NL4 explicitly requires three direct child substates of InMotion representing motion phases; no concurrent region language is used.

contracts.normative_statement: InMotion must have exactly three direct child substates: Accelerating, Cruising, Approaching.
contracts.quote: the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching
contracts.reason: NL4 explicitly counts three named substates owned by InMotion, establishing a direct_child_states cardinality obligation.

contracts.basis: NL5 'The system begins in the Accelerating substate'.

binding_hints.reason: InMotion owns the initial edge into its substates per NL4 discourse.
Accelerating is entered by the initial edge.

contracts.normative_statement: InMotion must have an initial pseudostate edge entering Accelerating.
contracts.quote: The system begins in the Accelerating substate
contracts.reason: NL5 establishes that within InMotion the first substate entered is Accelerating.

contracts.normative_statement: Accelerating must transition to Cruising once cruising speed is reached.
contracts.quote: moving to the Cruising substate once cruising speed is reached, as indicated by the "Reached Cruising/Cruise" signal
contracts.reason: NL5 states an explicit transition from Accelerating to Cruising triggered by reaching cruising speed.

binding_hints.reason: Accelerating is the stated origin per 'If the system is in the Accelerating substate'.

contracts.normative_statement: Accelerating must transition to Approaching upon approaching the destination.
contracts.quote: it transitions to the Approaching substate upon receiving the "Approached/Decelerate" signal
contracts.reason: NL6 states an explicit transition from Accelerating to Approaching.

contracts.normative_statement: Cruising must transition to Approaching upon approaching the destination.
contracts.quote: The system in the Cruising substate transitions to the Approaching substate when it approaches the destination, triggered by the "Approached/Decelerate" signal
contracts.reason: NL7 states an explicit transition from Cruising to Approaching.

binding_hints.reason: NL8 explicitly names the Entry lifecycle slot.

contracts.normative_statement: Accelerating must perform the Accelerate action on entry.
contracts.quote: The system enters the Accelerating substate when motion begins, marked by the "Entry/Accelerate" action
contracts.reason: NL8 supplies an exact state, entry phase, and action (Entry/Accelerate) satisfying the S4 lifecycle-action pattern.

contracts.normative_statement: Approaching must send the Send signal.
contracts.quote: the system sends the "Send" signal
contracts.reason: NL9 requires Approaching to send a Send signal, an independent effect obligation.

binding_hints.reason: Operating state required to continue its behavior.

contracts.normative_statement: Approaching must continue its approach behavior while active.
contracts.quote: and continues to approach the destination
contracts.reason: NL9 explicitly states the system continues to approach the destination while in Approaching, an explicit continuous operating obligation independent of the send-signal effect.

contracts.normative_statement: The system must remain in Approaching until it is ready to stop or decelerate.
contracts.quote: The system remains in the Approaching substate while nearing the destination, until it is ready to stop or decelerate
contracts.reason: NL10 explicitly requires the system to stay in Approaching until a stop/decelerate readiness condition, an exact state-retention obligation.

response.reason: Extracted atomic contracts preserving root-level initial entry into DoorsClosing, the DoorsClosing->InMotion endpoint and its trigger, InMotion's two alternative endpoints with guard/event distinctions and disjointness, EmergencyStopping's actions/effect, containment of InMotion's three substates, initial entry into Accelerating, sequential substate endpoints Accelerating->Cruising, Accelerating->Approaching, Cruising->Approaching (each with trigger/guard), the Entry/Accelerate lifecycle action, Approaching's Send effect, and Approaching's continuous state_action/retention obligation. Termination is not established anywhere since no segment states completion of the machine, so no termination contract was created. Every segment is covered by at least one contract.

segment_coverage.reason: Initial entry into DoorsClosing and endpoint to InMotion extracted.
Two alternative endpoints and disjointness extracted.
Emergency Stop action and Obstacle Detected effect extracted separately.
Three containment contracts plus one cardinality contract for InMotion substates.
unresolved_readings: Whether the three-substate count is best read as direct_child_states or explicit_named_members; both preserved.

segment_coverage.reason: InMotion-local initial entry into Accelerating and Accelerating->Cruising endpoint extracted.
Accelerating->Approaching endpoint extracted.
Cruising->Approaching endpoint extracted.
Entry/Accelerate lifecycle action extracted as S4-eligible state_action.
Send effect and continuous approach state_action extracted as independent obligations.
Explicit state-retention obligation for Approaching extracted.

alternatives.reason: NL1 states DoorsClosing transitions to InMotion triggered by the Closed/SendDeparted signal when doors are closed.

transition_groups.reason: Single transition from DoorsClosing to InMotion with a named triggering signal.

alternatives.reason: NL2 states InMotion transitions to Stopping on arrival, triggered by the Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived signal.
NL2 states InMotion alternatively transitions to EmergencyStopping if an obstacle is detected, treated as an event trigger.

transition_groups.reason: NL2 presents two either/or alternatives sharing source InMotion.

alternatives.reason: NL5 states Accelerating transitions to Cruising once cruising speed is reached, triggered by the Reached Cruising/Cruise signal.

response.reason: This lens cross-checks NL contract structure against the exact source inventory and closed FCSTM inventory for endpoint fidelity, owner-local initial entry, containment/cardinality, transition-group guard disjointness, and event-consumer coverage. Key findings: (1) InMotion has no owner-local initial pseudostate edge into Accelerating (NL5 initial_entry contract) - the FCSTM instead gives InMotion three unconditional/untriggered outgoing edges to Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching, none of which is a pseudo-initial edge, so the exact owner-local entry obligation is unsatisfied. (2) The InMotion->Stopping and InMotion->EmergencyStopping alternatives (NL2) are each triggered by distinct named events (Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived vs Obstacle_Detected) so they are not guard-disjointness violations - triggers are exact and distinct. (3) The Accelerating group (NL5/NL6) alternatives to Cruising and Approaching also carry distinct triggers (Reached_Cruising_Cruise vs Approached_Decelerate), so no disjointness issue there either. (4) Root initial entry to DoorsClosing exists and is exact (satisfied, omitted). (5) All explicit endpoint contracts NL1, NL2 (both), NL5, NL6, NL7 have exact matching edges in the closed model with correct source/target refs - satisfied, omitted. (6) Containment contracts NL4-CONTAIN-1/2/3 require Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching to be substates of InMotion, but the exact closed FCSTM models these as sibling top-level states (parent=llms_emp_feedback_final_0034, not InMotion) with only ordinary transitions from InMotion to each, not structural containment - this is a genuine containment mismatch. (7) Cardinality contract NL4-CARD-1 requires exactly 3 direct child substates of InMotion; owner is InMotion and member domain is explicit_named_members as recorded in the contract; the deterministic frontier will compare against the exact inventory. (2) The InMotion->Stopping and InMotion->EmergencyStopping alternatives (NL2) are each triggered by distinct named events (Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived vs Obstacle_Detected) so they are not guard-disjointness violations - triggers are exact and distinct. (3) The Accelerating group (NL5/NL6) alternatives to Cruising and Approaching also carry distinct triggers (Reached_Cruising_Cruise vs Approached_Decelerate), so no disjointness issue there either. (4) Root initial entry to DoorsClosing exists and is exact (satisfied, omitted). (5) All explicit endpoint contracts NL1, NL2 (both), NL5, NL6, NL7 have exact matching edges in the closed model with correct source/target refs - satisfied, omitted. (6) Containment contracts NL4-CONTAIN-1/2/3 require Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching to be substates of InMotion, but the exact closed FCSTM models these as sibling top-level states (parent=llms_emp_feedback_final_0034, not InMotion) with only ordinary transitions from InMotion to each, not structural containment - this is a genuine containment mismatch. (7) Cardinality contract NL4-CARD-1 requires exactly 3 direct child substates of InMotion; owner is InMotion and member domain is explicit_named_members as recorded in the contract; the deterministic frontier will compare against the exact inventory. (8) State-action contracts (NL3-ACTION-1, NL8-ACTION-1) have matching source carriers: the closed model shows EmergencyStopping enter abstract EmergencyStop, and Accelerating enter abstract Accelerate - action-completeness is a distinct property left to the behavior lens. (9) NL9-ACTION-1 progress claim and NL10 retention are behavior-lens territory, omitted here. Structural contrast findings emitted below.

response.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequence: root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, stable termination, dead-end/frontier facts, and cross-wrapper reachability using the closed FCSTM inspection-equivalent, verify, and SMT facts. Key findings: (1) Stopping (line:14) is a reachable leaf with zero outgoing transitions per LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING/W_DEADLOCK_LEAF diagnostics and verify_facts deadlock check 'refuted' -- this is exact deterministic frontier evidence usable as V1(initial_scope) supporting fact, though no supplied contract states an explicit progress/deadlock obligation for Stopping itself (NL contracts do not describe Stopping as an operating state requiring continuation), so it is preserved only as supporting basis rather than a standalone deadlock_freedom candidate absent an explicit progress contract. (2) The NL10 state_retention contract for Approaching requires remaining in Approaching "until ready to stop or decelerate" -- the closed model shows Approaching has two outgoing edges (Ready_to_Stop->Stopping, Destination_Missed->[*]), both of which are exact continuations consistent with the retention obligation (exit only on the named readiness signals), so this is satisfied and omitted. (3) NL9-ACTION-1 requires Approaching to progress/continue its approach behavior while active -- Approaching has outgoing transitions to Stopping and to final, consistent with continuation, so no deadlock issue there. (4) Root reachability: all 8 states are reachable_from_initial=true per inspection-equivalent facts, so no root-reachability defect exists for any named state. (5) Event-consumer coverage: every event_consumers entry shows reachable_consumer_state_refs equal to consumer_state_refs (full reachable coverage) for Closed_SendDeparted, Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived, Obstacle_Detected, Obstacle_Cleared, Reached_Cruising_Cruise, Approached_Decelerate, Ready_to_Stop, and Destination_Missed -- all declared consumers are reachable, so the derived event_consumption contracts (NL1/NL2/NL5/NL6/NL7-DERIVED) are satisfied and omitted. (6) Termination: EmergencyStopping and Approaching both have outgoing edges to [*] (final) per the FCSTM text and inspection-equivalent transitions (transition:line:31 EmergencyStopping->[*], transition:line:39 Approaching->[*]), matching canonical_source_ir final_states=[EmergencyStopping, Approaching]; no supplied contract designates a state_role=termination_state, so no termination candidate is derivable without inventing a role NL does not state. No supplied NL contract establishes forbidden-scope entry or bounded-response/trace obligations requiring an R1/R2/R3 candidate. Overall, deterministic facts show a healthy, fully-reachable, fully-consumed closed model with only the Stopping leaf lacking outgoing transitions, which is not tied to any explicit progress obligation in the supplied NL contracts, so it is recorded in basis rather than as an independent candidate.

decisions.basis: candidate/binding/plan/receipt for obligation 0034:r1:i0; S2 backend verdict=false; exact_source_inventory transitions tr_0006/tr_0009/tr_0011
decisions.reason: NL5 requires an owner-local initial pseudostate edge into Accelerating scoped to InMotion. The exact source and closed-model inventory (transitions tr_0006/tr_0009/tr_0011, lines 32/35/37) contain only three ordinary untriggered peer transitions to Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching, none of which is a declared initial pseudostate edge, and the backend receipt (S2, verdict=false) confirms no [*] -> Accelerating edge exists in InMotion's scope. The candidate's own rebuttal notes the untriggered edge coexists with two equally untriggered alternatives, so it cannot be uniquely read as the required default entry; the contract's exact initial-pseudostate requirement excludes this alternative, so the rebuttal is defeated by the same three-way symmetry the candidate itself identifies.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The untriggered InMotion->Accelerating transition (transition:line:32) could be read as an informal default-entry realization since it lacks a trigger like the other two edges.
decisions.violated_obligation: InMotion must have an owner-local initial pseudostate edge ([*] -> Accelerating) establishing Accelerating as the default-entry substate, per NL5.

decisions.basis: candidate/binding for obligation 0034:r1:i1; closed FCSTM inspection_equivalent_facts parent/is_composite fields
decisions.reason: NL4 requires Accelerating to be a substate contained within InMotion. The closed-model inspection_equivalent_facts explicitly record Accelerating's parent as the root machine 'llms_emp_feedback_final_0034', not InMotion, and InMotion is flagged is_composite=false with no children, so no structural containment relation exists. The candidate's proposed flattened-lowering rebuttal is directly excluded by these explicit parent/is_composite facts, which leave no room for an alternate containment reading; predicate unavailability (S1 not deciding containment) is a W-boundary matter only and does not erase this established source-level defect.

decisions.violated_obligation: Accelerating must be a nested child state within the InMotion composite/region per NL4.

(4) Root initial entry to DoorsClosing exists and is exact (satisfied, omitted). (6) Containment contracts NL4-CONTAIN-1/2/3 require Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching to be substates of InMotion, but the exact closed FCSTM models these as sibling top-level states (parent=llms_emp_feedback_final_0034, not InMotion) with only ordinary transitions from InMotion to each, not structural containment - this is a genuine containment mismatch. (7) Cardinality contract NL4-CARD-1 requires exactly 3 direct child substates of InMotion; owner is InMotion and member domain is explicit_named_members as recorded in the contract; the deterministic frontier will compare against the exact inventory. (8) State-action contracts (NL3-ACTION-1, NL8-ACTION-1) have matching source carriers: the closed model shows EmergencyStopping enter abstract EmergencyStop, and Accelerating enter abstract Accelerate - action-completeness is a distinct property left to the behavior lens. (9) NL9-ACTION-1 progress claim and NL10 retention are behavior-lens territory, omitted here. Structural contrast findings emitted below.

branches.reason: This lens audits behavioral consequence: root reachability, reachable event-consumer coverage, stable termination, dead-end/frontier facts, and cross-wrapper reachability using the closed FCSTM inspection-equivalent, verify, and SMT facts. Key findings: (1) Stopping (line:14) is a reachable leaf with zero outgoing transitions per LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING/W_DEADLOCK_LEAF diagnostics and verify_facts deadlock check 'refuted' -- this is exact deterministic frontier evidence usable as V1(initial_scope) supporting fact, though no supplied contract states an explicit progress/deadlock obligation for Stopping itself (NL contracts do not describe Stopping as an operating state requiring continuation), so it is preserved only as supporting basis rather than a standalone deadlock_freedom candidate absent an explicit progress contract. (2) The NL10 state_retention contract for Approaching requires remaining in Approaching "until ready to stop or decelerate" -- the closed model shows Approaching has two outgoing edges (Ready_to_Stop->Stopping, Destination_Missed->[*]), both of which are exact continuations consistent with the retention obligation (exit only on the named readiness signals), so this is satisfied and omitted. (3) NL9-ACTION-1 requires Approaching to progress/continue its approach behavior while active -- Approaching has outgoing transitions to Stopping and to final, consistent with continuation, so no deadlock issue there. (4) Root reachability: all 8 states are reachable_from_initial=true per inspection-equivalent facts, so no root-reachability defect exists for any named state. (5) Event-consumer coverage: every event_consumers entry shows reachable_consumer_state_refs equal to consumer_state_refs (full reachable coverage) for Closed_SendDeparted, Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived, Obstacle_Detected, Obstacle_Cleared, Reached_Cruising_Cruise, Approached_Decelerate, Ready_to_Stop, and Destination_Missed -- all declared consumers are reachable, so the derived event_consumption contracts (NL1/NL2/NL5/NL6/NL7-DERIVED) are satisfied and omitted. (6) Termination: EmergencyStopping and Approaching both have outgoing edges to [*] (final) per the FCSTM text and inspection-equivalent transitions (transition:line:31 EmergencyStopping->[*], transition:line:39 Approaching->[*]), matching canonical_source_ir final_states=[EmergencyStopping, Approaching]; no supplied contract designates a state_role=termination_state, so no termination candidate is derivable without inventing a role NL does not state. No supplied NL contract establishes forbidden-scope entry or bounded-response/trace obligations requiring an R1/R2/R3 candidate. Overall, deterministic facts show a healthy, fully-reachable, fully-consumed closed model with only the Stopping leaf lacking outgoing transitions, which is not tied to any explicit progress obligation in the supplied NL contracts, so it is recorded in basis rather than as an independent candidate.
